transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-06-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Leah Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Anita Rao (BlueHorizon CTO), Carlos Mendes (Lead ML Eng), Priya Shah (Head of Security)

Summary:
Short walk-through of Redwood's model catalog UI, filtering by open models, demo of benchmark comparisons and compatibility matrix for deployment types (hosted/dedicated/private). Customer wants clarity on model selection for clinical summarization use case and on-prem compatibility, quantization, and latency/throughput tradeoffs.

Topics: model catalog, benches, quantization, KV cache, routing policies, VPC/private deployment, SOC2

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Michael Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you taking time. I'm Michael from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Leah Ortiz, our solutions engineer. How's everybody doin'?
[00:06] Dr. Anita Rao: Good thanks. Excited to see the model catalog, we had a few questions based on the deck ya sent.
[00:09] Carlos Mendes: Hey team, time is tight so we'll try to keep Qs short. We're specifically interested in model selection for clinical summarization and de-identification, and we want to understand latency SLOs for 512 token outputs.
[00:18] Leah Ortiz: Awesome. We'll jump into the console, show the catalog filters (model family, license, token performance), and then open the benchmark comparison view. Quick note — the catalog lists open models like Llama2, Mistral, Falcon, RedPajama, and community fine-tunes we vet. Some names may show slightly different in transcribed notes, sorry, sometimes the autogenerated labels are off.
[00:36] Michael Chen: Right, and we'll show the compatibility matrix too — columns for hosted, dedicated (reserved GPU), and private/VPC on-prem. For each model we surface recommended quant profiles (8-bit, 4-bit QAT? and int8 where supported) and whether it passed our accuracy/regression tests on the clinical eval suite.
[00:50] Priya Shah: Can you clarify the SOC2 and key management approach? For private deployment we need HSM/KMS integration and audit logs retained for 7 years.
[00:58] Leah Ortiz: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSM via industry connectors). We also surface audit log retention policies in the console; longer retention is an add-on. We'll share the security whitepaper after the call.
[01:12] Carlos Mendes: On quantization — does Redwood do 4-bit out-of-the-box? Our experiments with 4-bit quantized Llama2 had some quality drop for clinical extraction.
[01:21] Leah Ortiz: We provide recommended quant profiles per model. For many models we have 8-bit and 4-bit int_quant variants; the catalog flags models where we saw measurable quality regression against the baseline. For clinical extraction we typically recommend mixed-precision or conservative 8-bit for Llama-family; Mistral often performs well with 4-bit in our bench, but it's workload dependent.
[01:40] Michael Chen: We also have model fallback routing — you can set policy to prefer hosted low-cost variants, but failover to a dedicated higher-accuracy instance if quality thresholds aren't met. That helps balance cost and SLA.
[01:53] Dr. Anita Rao: Can you show the benchmark chart? We need p50/p95/p99 for 64/256/512 tokens and also token-cost numbers.
[02:02] Leah Ortiz: Sure — opening the Benchmark view... (typing) Alright, here you can select a model set — I'm selecting Llama2-70b, Mistral-8x, Falcon-40b, and our curated redwood-vicuna-finetune — note the redwood-vicuna name in transcript might be off.
[02:19] Leah Ortiz: The chart shows latency distribution; p50 for 512 tokens on a 8xA100 dedicated node is ~210ms per token? Sorry, that's per request math, hmm let me rephrase — p50 end-to-end for a 512-token generation is about 420ms on dedicated optimized infra with batching of small sizes, p95 is ~780ms, p99 ~1.2s for that node. For hosted, multi-tenant endpoints you'll see slightly higher tail latency, and for Private on-prem numbers depend on your GPU class — e.g., 4xA100 setups will be different.
[02:46] Carlos Mendes: Those numbers seem optimistic, are you including tokenization and post-processing?
[02:49] Leah Ortiz: Yes, it's end-to-end measured from request start to final token. There is some variance in our internal bench depending on seq-len profiles and KV cache hit rates. Our console shows estimated token cost per model too, based on real infra runs.
[03:02] Michael Chen: We can export the benchmark spreadsheet, it includes per-model p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens — we'll send that after the call.
[03:09] Dr. Anita Rao: For private deployment, what's required for model compatibility? We have an on-prem cluster with Triton; can Redwood serve models there?
[03:16] Leah Ortiz: Redwood Private supports running our control plane in your VPC with a data plane that can be on-prem. We support Triton for certain models, but our recommended path is to run the Redwood data plane which orchestrates model variants and caching. We have a compatibility matrix that maps model formats (hf-pt, ggml, triton-onnx) to supported deployment modes.
[03:33] Priya Shah: Audit logs — can we push to our SIEM and set retention? Also want SSO/SAML integration.
[03:38] Michael Chen: Yes on both; SIEM forwarding via syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver is supported, and we do SAML/SCIM provisioning. We'll attach the configuration doc.
[03:46] Carlos Mendes: About KV cache — how does that work for chat histories? We're worried about memory blow-up for many long contexts.
[03:52] Leah Ortiz: Good question. KV cache is kept per conversation and we support prefix caching, partial KV eviction policies, and cross-request cache reuse for identical prefixes. For long contexts we recommend chunking and storing embeddings for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) rather than full KV retention; the console has settings to tune cache TTLs and max memory.
[04:12] Michael Chen: Also, Redwood Optimize gives recommendations — it looks at your workload, suggests batching profiles, cache TTLs, and quant profiles to save costs while maintaining your target quality. The Optimize tab shows expected cost delta if you change profiles.
[04:25] Dr. Anita Rao: Can you walk through a selection flow? Say we need a model that is permissively licensed, high precision for clinical text, and good latency.
[04:33] Leah Ortiz: In the catalog you can filter: license: permissive (MIT/Apache), accuracy: clinical eval pass, latency-tier: low, then sort by cost. That yields a short-list; we recommend running a pilot on your sample prompts. The compatibility matrix will also flag whether that model supports int8/4-bit and whether we have precomputed quantized artifacts.
[04:52] (Minor crosstalk)
[04:55] Carlos Mendes: For the pilot what's the typical duration and cost? We expect ~200K tokens/day for 2 weeks.
[04:59] Michael Chen: Pilot terms are flexible; for Dedicated you'd provision reserved capacity for the pilot window or run hosted with rate-limits. We can run a credit-backed hosted pilot for 2 weeks; Leah will scope the throughput run with your infra team.
[05:10] Priya Shah: Any data residency controls for hosted? We need EU-only for some teams.
[05:15] Leah Ortiz: Hosted has region controls; you can pin requests to EU regions. For strict residency, Private/VPC is recommended.
[05:21] Dr. Anita Rao: Ok, last thing — compatibility matrix, can you show the matrix export? We want to mail this to procurement.
[05:26] Leah Ortiz: Exporting now — it includes columns: model, license, hosted-yes/no, dedicated-yes/no, private-yes/no, quant-profiles, regression-flag, clinical-eval-score, recommended-hardware.
[05:36] Michael Chen: Great. Recap — Michael to send benchmark sheet and pricing, Leah to schedule throughput run and provide matrix export, BlueHorizon to share security contacts/questions. Any other blockers?
[05:46] Dr. Anita Rao: No blockers. We'll review the bench and circle back with final pilot decision.
[05:51] Michael Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with next steps in email. Appreciate it.
